items.stem: Construct a 3 × 4 matrix A = [aᵢⱼ] whose elements are given by aᵢⱼ = |−3i + j|/2.

items.answer: Columns of the first (3) ≠ rows of the second (2).

items.stem: If A = [3, 3, x + 4; 3, −3, 1; 1, y, 5] is a symmetric matrix, find x and y.

items.stem: Riya sends a two-letter code word to Kabir. Letters are numbered A = 1, B = 2, …, Z = 26; the word is written as a column X and sent as Y = KX with the key K = [1, 0; −1, −1]. Kabir receives Y = [15; −26]. (i) Find |K|. (ii) Find K⁻¹. (iii) Decode the word.
items.markingKey: (i) 1 mark (ii) 1 mark (iii) X = K⁻¹Y and letters (2 marks).

items.stem: Show that B = [−1, 1; −2, 3] is the inverse of A = [−3, 1; −2, 1].

items.stem: If a matrix has 9 elements, what are the possible orders it can have?
items.markingKey: Order m × n with mn = 9: 1 × 9, 3 × 3, 9 × 1.

items.stem: Find x and y if [x + y, 2; 5, xy] = [9, 2; 5, 8].

items.stem: Two stationery shops D and C in Agra sold pens, markers and rulers in a month as given by the matrix S = [350, 200, 290; 350, 140, 370] (rows: shops D, C; columns: pens, markers, rulers). items.markingKey: Revenue = S × P (column of selling prices) = [5380; 5460] (2 marks); profit = S × (P − C) = [2320; 2440] (2 marks); statement (1 mark).

items.stem: If A and B are matrices such that AB and BA are both defined, explain why AB and BA are square matrices.
items.answer: If A is m × n then B is n × m; AB is m × m and BA is n × n.
